html:
The Guanahatabey were an Indigenous people of far western Cuba at the time of European contact, at the western end of the island beyond the lands of the Taíno.

Spanish accounts from the conquest of Cuba in the 1510s describe them as people who lived by hunting, fishing and gathering, in caves or simple shelters, with a language the Taíno could not understand. Archaeologists see them as heirs of the older "Archaic" hunter-gatherers of the Caribbean, the Caribbean hunter-gatherers, although the evidence is thin. They are often confused with the Ciboney, who were a Taíno group.

They vanished soon after the Spanish conquest led by Diego Velázquez, through disease, forced labour and mixing. See also Guanahatabeyes.
sum: The Guanahatabey were an Indigenous people of far western Cuba at the time of European contact, at the western end of the island beyond the lands of the Taíno.
